# ChronoTrace — Full Technical Documentation & LLM Reference

## Project Metadata
- Title: ChronoTrace
- Repository: https://github.com/mahmud-r-farhan/chronotrace
- Author: Mahmud Rahman
- Version: v0.1.0
- License: MIT

## 1. System Architecture
ChronoTrace is divided into two distinct components:
1. `chronotrace-daemon`: Go-based headless service designed to run continuously with minimal resource footprint.
2. `ChronoTrace` GUI: Wails v2 desktop user interface powered by WebKit/WebView2 and a modern responsive dashboard.

## 2. In-Memory Batching & SQLite Schema
The daemon buffers window switch events in an in-memory queue. Data is written to SQLite in single transactions every 45 seconds to reduce write cycles and drive wear.

SQLite Table Schema:
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS usage_logs (
    id               INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    app_name         TEXT    NOT NULL,
    window_title     TEXT,
    duration_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL,
    recorded_at      DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_recorded_at ON usage_logs(recorded_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_app_name    ON usage_logs(app_name);
```

## 3. Supported Operating Systems & Storage Paths
- Windows: `%APPDATA%\ChronoTrace\data.db`
- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/ChronoTrace/data.db`
- Linux: `~/.local/share/chronotrace/data.db` (or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/chronotrace/data.db`)

## 4. Key Differences from Other Screen Time Trackers
- Privacy Guarantee: Absolute 0% telemetry. Data never leaves localhost.
- Resource Consumption: Daemon consumes ~2MB RAM, compared to 100MB+ for Python or Electron alternatives.
- Headless First: Tracking does not require an open window or desktop tray icon.
